chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Ali ibn Abd al-Rahim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man says to another man, “Come, I will sell to you with a good deal,” the profit is prohibited for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a seller's profit if he promises a 'good deal' to the buyer?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the prohibition of *ribh al-muwada'a* (profit from a guaranteed sale), where a seller's specific promise of a 'good deal' effectively guarantees the outcome, rendering the profit unlawful due to the element of certainty overriding risk. Scholars interpret 'hasan bi'ka' as a conditional guarantee that transforms the transaction from a standard sale into one with an embedded guarantee, thereby excluding the profit from the seller's permissible earnings. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and the avoidance of deceptive commercial practices that obscure true risk.
